new.name: Ralph W. Allen
new.description: Ralph W. Allen was a SNCC worker and one of the "Americus Four", arrested on August 8, 1963 after a demonstration in Americus, Georgia and charged under the state's capital "seditious conspiracy" statute — a charge that carried the death penalty and was used precisely because it allowed the denial of bail. He was held for approximately three months, until November 1, 1963, when a three-judge federal panel invalidated the charge. On November 6, 1963 an all-white jury convicted him of assault with intent to murder and imposed two years, pending appeal; the outcome of that appeal and any further custody are not established in the catalog record.

cases.sentence: Held without bail from August 8 to November 1, 1963 — approximately three months — until a three-judge federal panel invalidated the capital charge. updates.append: Braden was first prosecuted in 1954, when Kentucky charged him with sedition after he and his wife Anne helped an African American family, the Wades, purchase a house in a segregated Louisville neighborhood. He received fifteen years and served approximately eight months before obtaining an appeal bond; the conviction was overturned in 1956 after the Supreme Court's Nelson decision. He later served a separate one-year federal sentence in 1961 and 1962 for contempt of Congress, for refusing to answer the House Un-American Activities Committee.
